html:
SMTO-RST-0024 — SMTO's startup stalled while copying your saved data

GUID: 9fb27944-b8df-5bae-bba2-362b46fd6c09
Slug: controller-checkpoint-import-stalled
Domain: RST · Subsystem: controller

What happened

  • While starting, SMTO copies your saved data into a work area, and that copy stopped moving for five seconds, so SMTO didn't finish starting. Your saved data was left as it was.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Close programs that are working the disk hard, such as backups, virus scans or large file copies, then select Start again. SMTO stops the copy when the disk doesn't move it forward for five seconds, and a busy disk is a common reason.
  2. If SMTO's data is on a USB, external or network drive, make sure the drive is connected and responding, then select Start again. A drive that disconnects, sleeps or responds slowly makes the copy stall.
  3. If it stalls again, open Technical details and select Copy error details. The details show which saved database was being copied when it stalled.

What success looks like

  • The startup screen gets past Copying database and reaches Ready, and your conversations appear.

If it still fails

  • Send the copied details to the person who installed SMTO and say which drive holds the data. Don't delete the data folder or switch to an older copy of your data; this pause doesn't mean the data is damaged.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • During Controller recovery, the private staging copy of a committed SQLite database made no page progress for five seconds, so the copy was aborted, staging was removed and the Controller did not reach READY.

What this means

  • Controller recovery copies a retained database into private staging before migration and loading. The progress watchdog rejects copying that stops advancing. Copies that continue advancing may take longer than five seconds. Failure removes staging, prevents READY, and preserves the committed source and its receipts.

Why this can happen

  • SQLite backup callbacks reported no advancing page count for five seconds.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect disk responsiveness, storage contention and SQLite busy or locked conditions. A large database alone is not a stalled restore.

How to fix it

  • Check I/O latency and competing activity on the volume holding AOR_AGENT_STATE_DIR (for example iostat, dmesg, network or removable mount health) and make sure nothing holds a long lock on the source database, then restart the Server once storage is responsive. Preserve the committed checkpoint; this timeout does not establish corruption.
  • Check disk responsiveness and competing storage activity, then restart the Server after storage is responsive. Preserve the committed checkpoint; this timeout does not establish corruption.

Retry and execution caution

  • Storage is responsive and the Server can copy the retained database.

How to verify the fix

  • The startup copy advances to completion and the Controller reaches READY.

What not to do

  • Do not delete committed state, roll back to an older generation or replay completed work to clear this timeout.

Technical notes

  • The authoritative recovery generation remains unchanged. Do not delete or roll it back to clear a timeout.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.

Do not confuse with / related errors

  • SMTO-RST-0017 — SMTO couldn't open your saved data safely
